clue.text: Throw party, performing Blue Moon on dropping tab

parts.note: a disco is a dance party

indicators.note: the song title and tab are made to perform a new routine, so their letters are rearranged
the letters of 'on' are dropped from the mix before it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written: these two letters are removed

explanation.surface: Someone throws a party where the band plays Blue Moon after giving up on the bar tab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw' looks like part of 'throw a party', but it is the definition, meaning to confuse; 'on' does double duty in the surface as a preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone is to confuse or disconcert them, which is exactly what discombobulating means.

clue.text: In ladies' room at parties knocking down spirits?

indicators.note: read as a verb, 'parties' means the words go wild and break up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is in the ladies' room at parties, perhaps knocking back the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' suggests alcohol, but here it means morale; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Demoralisation is the act of crushing someone's morale, playfully described as knocking their spirits down.

clue.text: Steadier lassoes left by one more likely to snap

indicators.note: a lasso encircles its catch, so the steadier word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: surer means steadier, more sure-footed
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A steadier rider lassoes something, leaving one horse more likely to snap.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone surlier is grumpier and so quicker to snap irritably at others.

clue.text: Colours of crude undies donned by this person

parts.note: crude is unrefined oil

indicators.note: the underwear is put on by the speaker, so the speaker goes inside it

parts.note: pants are underwear in British English
the setter refers to themselves as I

explanation.surface: A setter confesses to wearing crude underwear in garish colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil paints are the pigments an artist uses, and painters commonly call their paints colours.

clue.text: Twirling aristocrat let go of hot guy here!

indicators.note: twirling spins the word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: a nob is an informal word for a toff or aristocrat
to fire an employee is to let them go

explanation.surface: A twirling aristocrat lets go of an attractive man at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hot guy' sounds like a handsome man, but the guy is Guy Fawkes, whose effigy is burnt each 5 November in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Effigies called guys are burnt on the fire on Bonfire Night, so this is where the guy gets hot.

clue.text: It augments strength of pub whisky no end

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: the whisky's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Bell's is a brand of blended Scotch whisky

explanation.surface: Someone claims a pub whisky boosts their strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbell is a weight bar lifted in training to build muscle power.

clue.text: Prone, racing, to go to topless

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off, as if its top were removed

parts.note: flying means moving very fast, racing

explanation.surface: A racer, flat out, decides to go topless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To go to' is a second route to the same letters: PLYING (travelling regularly to) loses its top too, so both phrases share 'topless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying means stretched out flat, which is what prone describes.

clue.text: Possessing will, still, to gather animals up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
to gather means to bring together within, so the cats go inside

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'yet more'
cats are animals

explanation.surface: Someone with a will still has to round up animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Testacy is the legal state of having made a valid will before death, the opposite of intestacy.

clue.text: Ready to grasp intimacy from another perspective

indicators.note: grasping holds something inside, so the phrase for intimacy sits within

parts.note: on hand means available, ready
'the other' is a British euphemism for sex

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to grasp at intimacy, considering a new angle.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom introduces a contrasting viewpoint, meaning considered another way.

clue.text: Republican occupying post yes-man vacated for Monroe

indicators.note: the Republican takes up residence inside the post

parts.note: mail is post

indicators.note: emptied of its middle, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Republican takes the job a yes-man left, in a scene about President Monroe.
explanation.walkthrough: Monroe suggests the US president, but it is the actress Marilyn Monroe.
explanation.definitionFit: Marilyn is the first name of the film star Marilyn Monroe.

clue.text: Checks possibly amber clothing at home

indicators.note: clothing wraps round, so the resin goes outside the other piece

parts.note: amber is fossilised resin, so resin is what amber may be
in means at home

explanation.surface: Checks, perhaps in amber, are worn about the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to restrain, as a rider pulls a horse back with the reins.

clue.text: Indian side's air shot getting cheers

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
ta is British slang for thanks, cheers

explanation.surface: An Indian team's misfired shot still earns applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' suggests a cricket team, but it is a side dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is a yoghurt accompaniment served alongside Indian dishes.

clue.text: Character from China is awful pig? Oh dear!

indicators.note: awful means terrible, so these letters are in bad order and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sees a badly drawn Chinese character and groans that it looks like a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese writing uses symbols that stand for ideas or words, known as ideographs.

clue.text: Might this be an allergy of the throat?

indicators.note: asks whether the letters could be rearranged into this form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor wonders whether a sore throat is an allergic reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Laryngeal is the adjective for the larynx, the voice box in the throat.

clue.text: Order for one sailor to make a U-turn

parts.note: say means for example, for one

indicators.note: a U-turn sends the word back the way it came

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor is ordered to turn the boat around.
explanation.definitionFit: A say-so is an authoritative instruction or permission, an order.

clue.text: Like a siren copper turned up, entering drug cutting area

indicators.note: the reversed copper symbol goes into the shortened drug
the area is cut out of the drug

parts.note: a sedative is a calming drug

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police siren sounds as a copper turns up at a drug raid in some neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: Siren suggests a police car, but it is the alluring woman of myth.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is an alluring temptress, so anything like her is enticing and seductive.

clue.text: Spots, or what's said to be spots

indicators.note: said signals that the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: sights are things you spot, scenic spots

explanation.surface: A spot-the-difference puzzle asks what counts as a spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses of spots are used: places (the definition) and things seen, sights, whose sound gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sites are places or locations, which are often called spots.

clue.text: What you may do with old car of Parisian ploughing into coach

definitions.text: What you may do with old car

indicators.note: the French word drives into the middle of the coach

parts.note: to coach is to train
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A Parisian's old car ploughs into a coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealers let you exchange an old vehicle as part-payment for a new one.

clue.text: It's obtained from Baker Street's west side with the cash we have

indicators.note: in an across answer the west side is the leftmost letter, so the first letter

parts.note: its first letter
dough is slang for cash, so the money that belongs to us is our dough

explanation.surface: Something got from Baker Street's west side, paid for with our own money.
explanation.walkthrough: Baker Street suggests Sherlock Holmes's London address, but the baker is just someone who bakes bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Sourdough is a tangy bread sold by bakers.

clue.text: Really gently, jogged round section of pitch

parts.note: so means really, as in 'so good'
p is piano, the musical marking for softly
ran is a past tense of run, jogged
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone jogged gently around part of a football pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitch suggests a sports field, but it is musical pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The soprano is the highest vocal range, a section of the pitch spectrum and of a choir.

clue.text: Sup rum with pastry one disliked after rising

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a tart is a pastry

explanation.surface: Someone drinks rum with a pastry after getting out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink to go with sup, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is a newcomer who has risen suddenly in status and is resented for arrogance.

clue.text: Offence of rum-running securing bishop a number of years

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the bishop safely inside
running means operating in a different order here, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
an age is a long period of years

explanation.surface: A bishop is caught up in a rum-smuggling offence for years.
explanation.definitionFit: To take umbrage is to take offence, feeling resentment at a slight.

clue.text: In backstreet, parent's waving arms in sacred place

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit in the reversed abbreviation

parts.note: street is ST, and 'back' turns it round to give TS

indicators.note: waving makes the letters move about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: In a backstreet, a parent waves their arms in a holy place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backstreet' splits into back + street: ST read backwards. 'Arms' suggests limbs, but a church transept forms the arms of its cross-shaped plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Transepts are the side wings crossing the nave of a cruciform church.

clue.text: Hedgehog thus keeps running

indicators.note: keeps in the sense of retains or holds, so the Latin word holds the running word within it

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus
on means running, as of a machine

explanation.surface: A hedgehog keeps on running, as hedgehogs do.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic the Hedgehog is the famously fast video-game character from Sega.

clue.text: One's tossed kind of red net away

indicators.note: away means the net is taken out

parts.note: Cabernet is a type of red wine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kind of red net is tossed away.
explanation.definitionFit: A caber is the long pole thrown in the Highland Games event, tossing the caber.

clue.text: Return of people keeping dry around cool, green region

indicators.note: return means the whole is read backwards
the AA goes around the cool word

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members stay off drink
in means fashionable, cool
eco means environmentally friendly, green

explanation.surface: People staying sober go back to a cool, verdant part of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceania is the geographic area of the Pacific islands including Australia and New Zealand.

clue.text: The greatest dessert for a legendary caveman

parts.note: the boxer Muhammad Ali called himself The Greatest
a baba is a rum-soaked sponge dessert

explanation.surface: The greatest pudding for a legendary cave dweller.
explanation.definitionFit: Ali Baba is the folk-tale hero who found the thieves' treasure in a cave.

clue.text: Scotch is a no-no for Rugby School's leader

parts.note: a knock-on, fumbling the ball forward, is an offence in rugby
the head is a school's head teacher

explanation.surface: Whisky is banned for the head of Rugby School.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch suggests whisky, but it is the verb meaning to put an end to; Rugby School is the English school where rugby began.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan is to quash it, and to knock it on the head means the same.
